nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

is an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services in India. It replaced several earlier indirect taxes and provides a common framework for taxation across the country. GST also enables eligible businesses to claim , subject to applicable conditions.
GST applies at different stages of the supply chain, with credit available for eligible taxes paid.
GST is generally collected based on the place of supply and consumption.
Different goods and services are subject to different GST rates as prescribed by law.
generally apply to intra-state supplies, while  applies to inter-state supplies.
Eligible businesses can claim credit for GST paid on purchases, subject to prescribed conditions.

Businesses must obtain GST registration when they cross the  or fall under a category requiring compulsory registration. Thresholds and exemptions vary based on the nature of supply, state, and other applicable conditions.
Taxpayers must file applicable GST returns and statements according to their registration and scheme.
E-invoicing applies to specified taxpayers meeting the prescribed turnover and other conditions.
Tax liabilities are generally paid electronically through the GST system.
Businesses should regularly reconcile books, invoices, returns, and ITC to identify discrepancies.
Managing multiple reporting requirements and deadlines.
Keeping track of changes in GST rules, rates, and procedures.
Matching purchase records with available GST data and eligible credits.
Errors in invoices, classification, tax rates, or returns may result in additional liability or other consequences.
Brings multiple indirect taxes under a common system.
Digital reporting and documentation improve transaction visibility.
Helps reduce cascading of taxes where credit is eligible.
Provides a standardized framework for taxation of supplies across states.
